title: Togo's Novissi program targeted rural emergency cash with machine learning on satellite imagery and mobile-phone data
summary: ML on satellite imagery and phone metadata set eligibility for Novissi rural cash; 138,531 beneficiaries paid, Nov 2020 to Aug 2021
account: The Government of Togo launched the Novissi emergency cash program on 8 April 2020. On 2 November 2020 it extended it to rural areas using a machine-learning pipeline built with UC Berkeley and IPA researchers. Satellite imagery produced poverty estimates for every canton to rank the poorest. Within eligible cantons a model trained on mobile-phone metadata predicted each subscriber's consumption to decide who was paid. Beneficiaries self-registered by USSD and received mobile-money installments of 8,170 CFA (women) or 7,000 CFA (men). The World Bank and Government of Togo report 138,531 rural beneficiaries from November 2020 to August 2021, funded by GiveDirectly (US$10 million). The Nature evaluation found phone-based targeting reduced exclusion errors by 4–21% relative to geographic alternatives.
purpose: Prioritize the poorest cantons and the poorest mobile subscribers within them for COVID-19 emergency cash transfers in the absence of a social registry.
system: Novissi rural targeting pipeline: satellite-imagery poverty maps for canton ranking plus supervised machine learning on anonymized mobile-phone call detail records for individual eligibility
model_version: gradient boosting regressor with Microsoft's LightGBM
developer: Innovations for Poverty Action, CEGA and UC Berkeley (Aiken and Blumenstock, UC Berkeley; Bellue, University of Mannheim; Karlan and Udry, Northwestern University) for the Government of Togo
deployer: Government of Togo, Ministry of Digital Economy and Transformation, with GiveDirectly
domain: Social protection and humanitarian cash transfers
taxonomy_note: The good for beneficiaries is emergency cash, and the type names the program's reach into rural areas with no registry.

ratings.reason: Five mobile-money installments of 8,170 CFA (women) or 7,000 CFA (men) to each of 138,531 rural beneficiaries during COVID-19 restrictions (World Bank study, Table 1).
The Government of Togo delivered shock-responsive rural assistance without a social registry. The World Bank documents the model as a reusable case study.
Material to many: 138,531 rural beneficiaries reached, and the Nature evaluation reports exclusion errors 4–21% lower than geographic targeting.

ai_role.statement: Decisive for who was paid: canton ranking and individual eligibility were both set by machine-learning predictions, while humans fixed the budget, thresholds and registration rules. The Nature evaluation is co-authored by the team that built the targeting method. The World Bank/Government of Togo case study is independent of the developers.

evidence.citation: Aiken, E., Bellue, S., Karlan, D., Udry, C., Blumenstock, J. E. (2022). Machine learning and phone data can improve targeting of humanitarian aid. Nature 603, 864–870 (the quotation is the Extended Data Fig. 1 caption, panel a, with its reference markers omitted).
evidence.title: Machine learning and phone data can improve targeting of humanitarian aid
evidence.quote: Satellite imagery of Togo is used to construct micro-estimates of poverty (middle), which are overlayed with population data to produce canton-level estimates of wealth.

evidence.citation: Lawson, C., Koudeka, M., Cárdenas Martínez, A. L., Alberro Encinas, L. I., George Karippacheril, T. (2023). Novissi Togo: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence to Deliver Shock-Responsive Social Protection. World Bank and Government of Togo, Social Protection and Jobs Discussion Paper No. 2306, September 2023 (month only; first day used).
evidence.title: Novissi Togo: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence to Deliver Shock-Responsive Social Protection
evidence.quote: Subsequently, the program was extended on November 2, 2020, to rural areas with a high prevalence of poverty (henceforth referred to as model 2).

evidence.citation: GiveDirectly (2021). Innovations in Togo and the future of cash distribution. GiveDirectly, The Future of Cash, published 20 April 2021 (implementing partner and funder, not the AI developer).
evidence.title: Innovations in Togo and the future of cash distribution
evidence.quote: Leveraging machine learning in combination with satellite imagery and cell phone metadata, the program was able to identify those living in extreme poverty

produced_by: Consumption model trained on mobile-phone metadata with a recent phone survey as ground truth
USSD self-registration and mobile-money payment rails
must_hold: Target population owns and uses mobile phones (non-subscribers are excluded by design)
Operators provide anonymized call detail records
Recent ground-truth survey available for training

echoes.setting: Nigeria Rapid Response Register: ML poverty maps from satellite imagery selected 1,163 poorest urban wards for COVID-19 cash (month only known; first day used)
echoes.source: Date: Human Rights Watch (2021) 'began in January 2021', https://www.hrw.org/report/2021/07/28/between-hunger-and-the-virus/the-impact-of-the-covid-19-pandemic-on-people-living, and Smythe and Blumenstock (2022) PNAS 'mid-January 2021', https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9371736/; ward count: World Bank (2021) PAD P176935, https://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/717321706545772846/pdf/Nigeria-National-Social-Safety-Net-Program-Scale-Up-Project.pdf (the PAD itself dates the USSD self-registration launch to June 2021)

paired_incident.title: Algorithm to Distribute Social Welfare Reported for Oversimplifying Economic Vulnerability
paired_incident.basis: World Bank-backed poverty-targeting algorithm for cash transfers oversimplified household vulnerability, excluding poor Jordanians; Novissi used the same machine-learning targeting of the poor.

headline: Novissi targeting pays 138,531 rural beneficiaries in Togo
metric: reduced exclusion errors by 4–21% relative to geographic alternatives

comparator.against: the geographic targeting options considered by the Government of Togo
comparator.before: errors of exclusion of 59%–78% for the feasible alternatives
comparator.after: errors of exclusion of 53% for the phone-based approach, a reduction of 4–21%
comparator.quote: Relative to the geographic targeting options considered by the Government of Togo, the machine-learning approach reduces errors of exclusion by 4–21%.
